claims.proposition_evaluated: The $100 million approved in December 2022 for capital profile CM-20-0330 was almost double Edmonton's annual Snow and Ice Control budget in force on 2022-12-12.
claims.interpretation_notes: I treated the July 4, 2022 one-time $4.700 million increase as part of the approved 2022 gross Snow and Ice Control expenditure budget in force on the comparison date. The original gross budget was $64.466 million, so the amended gross denominator was $69.166 million. The ratio is $100 million / $69.166 million = 1.4458, below the brief's 1.5 threshold and therefore Contradicted. Excluding the amendment would produce 1.5512 and Partially supported. Using the original $63.653 million net operating requirement produces 1.5710 and Partially supported, but that is not the required gross denominator and the $4.700 million reserve funding was not tax levy. Under the brief's alternative cutoffs, 1.4458 is Partially supported. The exact December 2022-approved 2023 gross cell could not be extracted reliably from the authoritative attachment; the later amended 2023 gross budget of $63.574 million is not a substitute.

supporting_evidence.finding: The adopted capital budget prints CM-20-0330 in thousands as 2023 $5,950; 2024 $26,750; 2025 $33,650; 2026 $33,650; total $100,000. The approved average is $25.000 million per year.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The capital-program numerator, its four-year period and annual allocations.

supporting_evidence.finding: The original 2022 Snow and Ice Control table, printed in thousands on page 212, gives gross expenditure and transfers of $64,466 and a total net operating requirement of $63,653.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The original approved 2022 gross and net Snow and Ice Control budgets before the July 2022 amendment.

supporting_evidence.finding: Council's December 2022 amendment funded enhanced snow standards by $4.0426 million in 2023, $3.7248 million in 2024, $2.4768 million in 2025 and $0.7214 million in 2026.
supporting_evidence.source_title: City Council budget minutes, Operating Budget Amendment 18
supporting_evidence.establishes: The enhancement approved for the 2023-2026 snow program, while not by itself establishing each year's full program budget.

challenging_evidence.establishes: The in-year amendment that raises the primary gross denominator to $69.166 million and lowers the ratio to 1.4458.

challenging_evidence.finding: For 2023, the later adjusted Snow and Ice Control budget was $63.574 million gross and actual gross expenditure was $54.917 million; actual revenue was $2.362 million and the actual net position was $52.555 million.

challenging_evidence.establishes: The 2023 actual expenditure and later adjusted budget, not the December 2022-approved denominator.

challenging_evidence.finding: CM-20-0330 actual expenditure was $0.807 million in 2023. Cumulative actuals were $10.496 million at 2024 year-end and $25.093 million at 2025-09-30, giving annual 2024 actual of $9.689 million and January-September 2025 actual of $14.597 million. The completed-year 2023-2024 average was $5.248 million.
challenging_evidence.source_title: Capital Financial Updates for 2023, 2024 and September 2025
challenging_evidence.establishes: Actual capital expenditure was far below the four-year approved amount; approved funding must not be described as money already spent.

challenging_evidence.finding: Using aligned 2023 actuals, $0.807 million of CM-20-0330 expenditure divided by $54.917 million of snow expenditure is 0.0147, or 1.47%.
challenging_evidence.establishes: The actual-spending comparison for 2023, which is a qualification rather than the verdict basis.

limitations: The authoritative CO01733 Attachment 2 table was located, but its exact 2022-2026 cells were not exposed reliably by the public portal's indexed text.
The final December 2022-approved 2023 gross denominator and the four-year approved snow total therefore could not be reported without risking transcription error.

A 2025 year-end capital report exists, but the CM-20-0330 row could not be extracted reliably; $14.597 million is only January through September.

what_would_change_my_verdict: An authoritative accounting showing that the July 4, 2022 $4.700 million increase did not increase the program's approved gross expenditure budget would change the primary result to Partially supported.

claims.suggested_one_line: Contradicted on the frozen primary reading: the $100 million four-year capital approval was 1.45 times the amended 2022 gross snow budget, not almost double.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Council approved $100 million over four years for CM-20-0330. Edmonton's original 2022 gross snow budget was $64.466 million, and council added $4.700 million before the claim was made, bringing the in-force gross budget to $69.166 million. The resulting 1.45 ratio falls below the brief's 1.5 cutoff.
suggested_tldr: $100 million was a four-year capital approval, not annual spending.
The amended 2022 gross snow budget was $69.166 million, giving a ratio of 1.45.
Actual CM-20-0330 spending through September 2025 was $25.093 million.

claims.proposition_evaluated: Under the brief's roads-only profile boundary, Edmonton's adopted 2023-2026 capital budget allocated about $1.8 billion to roads, approximately eighteen times the $100 million allocated to CM-20-0330.
claims.interpretation_notes: The captured quotation said '180 times,' but $1.8 billion divided by $100 million is 18, and the normalized proposition tests that implied ratio. The primary roads-only sum is $1.945703 billion, or 19.457 times $100 million, meeting both the $1.5 billion primary and $1.62 billion alternative Supported thresholds. Appendix A figures are printed in $000s. Profiles summed, with Appendix A index pages, were: 18-66-6503 $94.202m p.102; 19-22-9006 $119.200m plus $41.821m p.103; 21-20-9301 $54.634m p.103; 21-20-9302 $54.597m p.103; 21-40-9031 $0.012m p.103; 21-40-9032 $0.010m p.102; 22-22-9700 $10.056m p.101; 22-22-9701 $5.094m p.102; CM-20-2020 $9.007m p.103; CM-22-0000 $64.843m p.103; CM-24-0000 $209.836m p.103; CM-26-0000 $9.308m p.103; CM-66-2194 $0.720m p.103; CM-66-2525 $16.000m p.103; CM-66-2585 $25.875m p.100; CM-66-2596 $17.148m p.100; CM-99-0060 $7.914m p.103; CM-99-9600 $376.255m p.103; 20-40-9017 $4.658m p.100; 20-40-9019 $0.721m p.100; 21-40-9023 $14.652m p.100; 21-40-9024 $22.047m p.100; 21-40-9025 $9.780m p.100; 21-40-9026 $2.100m p.100; 21-40-9027 $0.464m p.100; 22-40-9028 $17.130m p.100; 22-40-9029 $23.710m p.100; CM-25-0000 $545.717m p.100; CM-27-0000 $81.310m p.100; 23-24-0300 $97.000m p.102; 21-24-9301 $9.832m p.102; and 21-24-9302 $0.050m p.102. The last three bridge sheets have no Service Category; no other editor-list label mismatch was found. The required alternative is Table 8's combined Active Pathways and Roads Service total of $1.7940 billion, or 17.94 times, also Supported under both cutoff sets. The narrow Roads-labelled set is $1.116532 billion, or 11.165 times, and is Partially supported under both cutoff sets. The widest reading is $2.025848 billion, or 20.258 times, and is Supported.
